items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It was interesting and educational to play with Bird.

ctx.x: Sure. How about playing with him?

How about playing with him? Charlie Parker was such a genius that playing with him could be an intimidating experience and was an intimidating experience. You wondered what could you do that would be on the same level with what he had just done, and invariably he would play first. [laughs] Oh, boy. It left you in pretty bad shape. It was interesting and educational to play with Bird.

Around this time was when you also met Dizzy Gillespie and began doing some infrequent sitting in with his group. Could you talk a little bit about your recollections and impressions of Dizzy Gillespie, both with the long personal relationship you had with him as well as Dizzy the musician.
